main_body: A flat sand-coloured ground patch (4x3 tiles, 48x16 px) with sparse lighter and darker speckles and one small grey stone and one pink flower. Terrain tile, no standing volume.
top_band: none (flat ground texture; column scan shows only speckle variation of the same sand tone, no top band or front face)
evidence: Terrain ground patch seen from above; it is not a standing object, so the top/front contract does not apply. Column scans show a uniform sand tone (L=198) with a few speckle pixels (L=220 and L=169), with no structure of a raised volume. The drawing matches the terrain kind and has no side faces or elevation problems.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 3 colours per tile, against 26 for the reference grass and 7 for the paving (80 distinct colours for the grass). The sand has essentially three lightness steps: base #e2c584, light #f1dca2 and dark #c9a666, plus a grey stone and a pink flower. Speckles are sparse single pixels, so the base colour stays as large flat areas (10% flat-fill coverage versus 0% for both references). There are no outlines, as is normal for ground. Beodeul's grass has several greens, clumps and tufts, so this sand looks thinner and flatter next to it. It lacks the grain, pebble clusters and ripple variation needed for equal richness.
